title: Simulation Task
description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Contains demographic and behavioral attributes of each agent, including age, occupation, risk perception, and social connection counts
data_files.social_network.json: Contains structured data representing a social network. Each entry corresponds to a user (identified by a unique integer ID), and the values describe the different types of relationships that user has with others. Data Structure: The top-level structure is a dictionary ({} in JSON). Keys: Each key is a unique user ID (as an integer, e.g., 0, 1, 2, etc.). Values: Each value is another dictionary with the following fields: "family": a list of user IDs representing family connections. "work_school": a list of user IDs representing colleagues or schoolmates. "community": a list of user IDs representing community-level acquaintances. "all": a merged list of all user IDs connected to the user across the three categories above.
data_files.train_data.csv: Time series data for the first 30 days, used for training the model

RMSE.description: Root Mean Square Error measuring overall predictive accuracy of mask adoption rates
RMSE.interpretation: Directly interpretable as percentage deviations due to the 0-1 range

interactions.name: peer_influence
interactions.description: Neighbors in the social network influence each other's mask-wearing via tie strength, trust, and observed adoption; can be threshold-based or probabilistic contagion.

interactions.name: location_norm_observation
interactions.description: Individuals observe the proportion of mask-wearers at locations and update perceived norms and utility of wearing.

interactions.name: policy_announcement
interactions.description: Authority issues mandates or recommendations that alter perceived costs/benefits and compliance behavior.

interactions.name: policy_enforcement
interactions.description: Locations and/or authority enforce mandates with some probability, applying fines or access restrictions.

interactions.name: public_messaging
interactions.description: Broadcast campaigns increase awareness and adjust perceived benefits and risk perception.

interactions.name: network_rewiring
interactions.description: Agents may strengthen ties with similar mask behavior (homophily) or weaken ties with dissimilar peers over time.

metrics.name: overall_adoption_rate_over_time
metrics.description: Fraction of agents wearing masks at each time step.

metrics.name: final_adoption_rate
metrics.description: Adoption fraction at the end of the simulation period.

metrics.name: time_to_50_percent_adoption
metrics.description: Number of days until 50% of agents adopt mask-wearing.

metrics.name: time_to_peak_adoption
metrics.description: Day with the highest adoption level.

metrics.name: adoption_by_degree_quantile
metrics.description: Adoption rates stratified by agents' network degree quantiles.

metrics.name: cascade_size_distribution
metrics.description: Distribution of connected adoption cascades triggered by initial adopters.

metrics.name: policy_attribution_fraction
metrics.description: Share of adoption events primarily attributable to policy/enforcement vs peer influence.

metrics.name: norm_churn_rate
metrics.description: Rate at which agents switch between wearing and not wearing over time.

metrics.name: group_inequality_in_adoption
metrics.description: Difference or Gini index of adoption across demographic or location groups.

metrics.name: location_norms_vs_adoption_correlation
metrics.description: Correlation between observed location norms and individual adoption.

validation_criteria.name: s_shaped_diffusion_curve
validation_criteria.description: Aggregate adoption exhibits an S-shaped curve under threshold contagion assumptions.

validation_criteria.name: policy_effect_monotonicity
validation_criteria.description: Higher enforcement probability or campaign intensity weakly increases adoption, holding other factors constant.

validation_criteria.name: complex_contagion_signature
validation_criteria.description: With higher adoption thresholds, greater clustering increases adoption likelihood (consistent with complex contagion literature).

validation_criteria.name: no_influence_stability
validation_criteria.description: With zero peer and authority influence, adoption remains near the initial level over time.

validation_criteria.name: bounded_outcomes
validation_criteria.description: Adoption rates remain within [0,1] and simulation variables remain finite.

validation_criteria.name: steady_state_or_periodicity
validation_criteria.description: System either converges to a steady adoption level or shows bounded periodic behavior by end of simulation.
